title: Dodge Dakota Engines by Year (1987–2011)
description: Every factory engine in the Dodge Dakota by year, 1987–2011: the 2.2 and 2.5 fours, the 3.9 V6, 5.2 and 5.9 Magnum V8s, the Shelby and R/T, and the 3.7 and 4.7.
intro: Dodge's midsize Dakota pickup ran from 1987 to 2011, sold as the Ram Dakota for its final year. It was the first midsize pickup offered with a V8.
Pick a year to see every engine offered that model year, with its code, rated horsepower and the trims it came in. Each engine links to its full specs.
The first Dakota used the 2.2 and 2.5 fours and the 3.9 V6, then the 5.2 V8 from 1991 and Magnum engines from 1992. The 1989 Shelby Dakota had a 5.2 V8.
The second Dakota offered the 2.5 four, the 3.9 V6, the 5.2 and, in the 1998–2003 R/T, the 5.9 V8, with the 4.7 V8 from 2000 and the 3.7 V6 for 2004.
The last Dakota used the 3.7 V6 and the 4.7 V8, with a high-output 4.7 through 2007.

excluded.name: 2.5L / 153 inline-four
excluded.researchNote: Only NHRA lists a 2.5 in the 1988 Dakota. EPA has only the 2.2 for 1988 and Wikipedia dates the 2.5 from 1989; Flory's 1988 table lists a 153 CID TBI 96 @ 4400 but the snippet does not tie it to the Dakota (the Caravan used it). Probably NHRA carrying the 1989 engine back a year; hp withheld.

method: Every engine and year listed here was confirmed by at least three independent sources: the NHRA Stock Car Classification Guides, factory material such as GM Heritage Center information kits and sales brochures, EPA records and established references. Several Wikipedia articles count as one source. Where sources give different ratings, the factory figure is shown and the difference is noted. Factory race-only packages need two sources.
